answer: Each identity stakes 80 credits on one harbor crane, sealed with a lantern seal binding crane, voyage and key. It posts each voyage lift log to a harbor lift board; auditors recompute tonnage from its load log, cross-check lantern lamp-hours, and burn the bond on any mismatch over 2 percent or reused seal or log. First calibration costs 37 credits; the k-th costs 37+4(k-1), the 1000th 4033, and 1000 fakes 2,035,000 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-crane ring fails: one seal cannot cover two keys, and copied logs burn all bonds. An honest operator pays 37 once, refunded if clean.
